quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check the inside rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder. Make sure it is safe before you move.

questions.question: How can you avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. You do not know what is ahead. Braking on a curve can cause you to skid.

questions.question: How can drivers see objects in their blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Only the left outside mirror.
Over their left or right shoulder.
Only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over their left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Your blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Stop sign ahead.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is slippery and dangerous when wet. Slow down when you see wet pavement because it takes longer to stop.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Treat the light like a stop sign.
Wait until the light turns green to proceed.
Continue through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the light like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light the same way as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving at night, what should you do?

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase the distance between your car and the car ahead when it is dark. Use your headlights properly. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights because the glare can blind you.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Treat the light like a stop sign.
Wait until the light turns green to proceed.
Slow down and proceed with caution through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution through the intersection.
questions.explanation: Slow down and proceed with caution at a flashing yellow light. You do not need to stop unless it is unsafe to go.

questions.question: What happens to fines for moving traffic violations in work zones?

options.text: Lessened.
Doubled.
Non-existent.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doubled.
questions.explanation: In Arkansas, fines for moving traffic violations in highway work zones are doubled when workers are present and warning signs are posted.

questions.question: The driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Cautiously pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.
Stop, proceeding only when all the pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, proceeding only when all the pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk. Pedestrians you cannot see may be crossing. Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have crossed.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not permitted?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near any curve or hill.
On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near any curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians and may cause a crash.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: It is safe to use your cruise control.
Make speed and directional changes more gradually than you would otherwise.
Drive as you would under normal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make speed and directional changes more gradually than you would otherwise.
questions.explanation: Make speed and directional changes slowly on snow or ice. Do not use cruise control because your tires may lose contact with the road and you will lose control.

questions.question: Before you enter an intersection, which way should you look?

options.text: Left, your right, then your left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, your right, then your left again.
questions.explanation: Look left, then right, then left again before entering an intersection. Look for approaching vehicles and pedestrians. Look left again because vehicles from your left are closer. Make sure the path is clear all the way across.

questions.question: Before you change lanes, what should you do besides check your mirrors?

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your traffic lane.
Glance over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes. This ensures you will not hit a vehicle in the lane you want to enter and that no other driver is moving into the same spot.

questions.question: Bright headlights from an oncoming car are blinding you at night. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right edge of the road instead of straight ahead. This keeps your vehicle on the road safely until you pass the oncoming car.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at accidents or unusual events does what?

options.text: Causes traffic congestion.
Prevents rear-end collisions.
Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes traffic congestion.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at accidents or unusual events. This is called "rubbernecking" and it causes traffic congestion.

questions.question: You want to pass a pedestrian walking on the road. An oncoming car is approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming car pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at a steady speed. The oncoming car must stop for you.
Honk your horn to get the pedestrian to move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming car pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Slow down and let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is using its siren and flashing lights. How should you give it the right-of-way?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. You can move again after the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.question: Where can you safely pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection with no oncoming vehicles
Where signs and pavement markings allow passing
In a curve with no oncoming vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Where signs and pavement markings allow passing
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections or other crossing points like parking lots and alleys. Do not pass on curves or hills where you cannot see oncoming traffic. Only pass where signs and pavement markings permit it, and only if you have enough space.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: Motorcycles do not follow the same rules as other vehicles.
Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
Motorcycles brake more slowly than regular vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop quickly. If you follow too closely, you will not have time to stop if the motorcycle suddenly stops. You need space to avoid a crash.

questions.question: Should you always drive more slowly than other cars?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is good defensive driving.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Slow down in heavy traffic or bad weather. But do not drive so slowly that you block normal traffic movement. You can be cited for this.

questions.question: You come to an intersection with a flashing yellow light. What must you do?

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. Watch for crossing traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: You see this sign for a railroad crossing with no signal. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep a steady speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Look both ways and listen for trains. Be ready to stop if a train is coming. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: Driving slower than surrounding traffic is:

options.text: A good idea in bad weather.
Okay if you do not know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because other drivers may try to pass you unsafely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because other drivers may try to pass you unsafely.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be dangerous. Drivers behind you may become impatient and take risky chances to pass you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road gets wider ahead.
The right lane ends soon. Merge left.
Highway entrance ramp ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends soon. Merge left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you that a lane is closing ahead. Traffic must merge to the left.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Yield to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts drivers that bicycles may be crossing in this area.
